quizzes.title: Repo Rate and the Economy: Practice Set
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank responsible for managing the country's financial system. Its roles include acting as the monetary authority, lender of last resort, banker to the government and custodian of foreign exchange reserves, and it aims to maintain price stability while promoting economic growth. Its supervisory role covers issuing bank licences and inspecting commercial banks. The Repo Rate is one of the main instruments of monetary policy used by the RBI. Because it governs the cost at which money moves between the central bank and commercial banks, changes to it affect banks and borrowers across the economy. The rate is decided by the Monetary Policy Committee, which must meet at least four times each year and takes its decisions by majority vote. Recently, the Committee chose to keep the policy rate steady as tensions in West Asia rose. These tensions have made global energy prices and trade flows more volatile, and India is experiencing a supply-side shock linked to global energy and commodity markets. Such shocks can raise input costs and prices even without excess domestic demand. Retail inflation has stayed within the mandated target band, and core inflation, which excludes food and fuel, has remained stable. The overall stance is described as cautious and steady.

questions.q: In December 2025, by how many basis points did the RBI cut the Repo Rate?
questions.explanation: The booklet records the December 2025 cut as 25 basis points, to 5.25%.

questions.q: What was the total reduction in the Repo Rate by the RBI during 2025, in basis points?
questions.explanation: The booklet says the December 2025 cut marked the fourth reduction of 2025, totalling 125 basis points.

questions.q: According to the booklet, a higher Repo Rate slows which two things in the economy?
questions.explanation: A higher Repo Rate slows down investment and the money supply in the market.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Lowering the Repo Rate tends to increase borrowing and spending in the economy.
Reason (R): A lower Repo Rate makes loans cheaper for banks and lowers interest rates for borrowers.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cheaper loans and lower rates for borrowers are the mechanism that leads to increased borrowing and spending.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Higher Repo Rate   ->   D. Raises the Repo Rate
II. Lower Repo Rate   ->   A. Lowers the Repo Rate
III. RBI's response to high inflation   ->   B. Curbs excessive spending
IV. RBI needs to pump funds into the economy   ->   C. Increases overall supply of money
questions.explanation: A higher Repo Rate curbs excessive spending, a lower one increases money supply, high inflation calls for a raised Repo Rate, and pumping funds means lowering it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Repo Rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks.
II. A higher Repo Rate makes loans cheaper for commercial banks.
III. The Repo Rate is set by the Monetary Policy Committee.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is reversed, since a higher Repo Rate makes loans costlier for banks, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Repo stands for 'Repurchasing Option' or 'Repurchase Agreement'.
II. The December 2025 cut was the second reduction by the RBI.
III. A lower Repo Rate makes loans costlier for banks.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, because the December 2025 cut was the fourth reduction and a lower Repo Rate makes loans cheaper.

quizzes.title: Repo Rate and the Economy: Short Answer
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India, which is the country's central bank, manages the financial system through several tools. One of the most watched is the Repo Rate, the rate that acts as the cost of money for the banking system. Changes to this rate travel through the economy. When the rate is set higher, banks face costlier loans, and interest rates for consumers and businesses rise as well. Spending and investment tend to slow in such a situation. When the rate is eased, borrowing becomes cheaper and the overall supply of money in the economy increases, which can help growth. The Monetary Policy Committee decides the rate, and its decisions are based on a majority vote. The Committee meets at least four times each year. In its most recent review, the Committee chose to keep the rate unchanged, as geopolitical tensions in West Asia raised uncertainty about energy prices and trade. Supply-side shocks from global energy and commodity markets can also raise prices without reflecting excess demand. The RBI's role in the financial system is wide, covering monetary authority, supervision of banks, banker to the government and custodian of reserves. The rate is one of several instruments that the RBI can use at different times, depending on conditions in the economy. The aim of policy is to balance price stability with support for economic growth.

questions.q: In which month and year did the RBI cut the Repo Rate by 25 basis points to 5.25%?
questions.explanation: The booklet dates the 25 basis point cut to December 2025.

questions.q: What do the letters 'Repo' stand for? (two words)
questions.explanation: Repo stands for Repurchasing Option or Repurchase Agreement.

questions.q: The December 2025 cut was which numbered reduction by the RBI? (word or numeral)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the December 2025 cut marked the 4th reduction by the RBI.

questions.q: What was the total reduction in the Repo Rate by the RBI in 2025, in basis points? (number)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the 2025 reductions totalled 125 basis points.

questions.q: What does a higher Repo Rate do to excessive spending? (one word)
questions.explanation: A higher Repo Rate curbs excessive spending and slows investment.

questions.q: What does the RBI do to the Repo Rate when it needs to pump funds into the economy? (one word)
questions.explanation: When the RBI needs to pump funds into the economy, it lowers the Repo Rate.

questions.q: High levels of what lead the RBI to raise the Repo Rate? (one word)
questions.explanation: During high levels of inflation, the RBI raises the Repo Rate to bring down the flow of money.

quizzes.title: Inflation Targeting and the RBI: Practice Set
quizzes.passage: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank responsible for managing the country's financial system. Its concept drew on the ideas in Dr. Ambedkar's book on the rupee, and the Hilton Young Commission recommended that it be established. The British government passed the Reserve Bank of India Act, and the institution was later nationalised after having been privately owned. Today the RBI performs several roles. As a supervisor, it can issue bank licences, open branches, set minimum reserves and inspect commercial banks. As a monetary authority, it issues and destroys currency notes and circulates coins minted by the government. It also manages the financial operations of the Central Government under the RBI Act, and it regulates the forex market through exchange rules. The Monetary Policy Committee sets the benchmark policy rate needed to contain inflation within the specified target level. The RBI's first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith, and its first Indian Governor was C.D. Deshmukh. Several of these functions are carried out under the RBI Act. Its work is therefore wide in scope, touching the banking sector, the government and the foreign exchange market alike. These responsibilities together make the RBI a central institution in India's financial life.

questions.q: In which year did India adopt Flexible Inflation Targeting?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that India adopted Flexible Inflation Targeting in 2016.

questions.q: What is the permitted deviation from India's 4% inflation target?
questions.explanation: India's inflation target of 4% carries a deviation of plus or minus 2%.

questions.q: Which RBI role involves managing India's foreign exchange reserves?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists custody of India's foreign exchange reserves as one of the RBI's roles.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The RBI works to maintain price stability while promoting economic growth.
Reason (R): Inflation targeting aims to keep inflation within a pre-defined range.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the definition of inflation targeting does not explain the RBI's dual objective.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Urjit Patel Committee (2014)   ->   A. Target set every five years with the RBI
II. Chakravarty Committee   ->   D. Mandated band of 2 to 6 per cent
III. Retail inflation band   ->   B. Formalised inflation targeting in 2014
IV. Frequency of review of the target   ->   C. First proposed 4% target with 2% band
questions.explanation: The Urjit Patel Committee formalised inflation targeting, the Chakravarty Committee first proposed the 4% target, the retail band is 2 to 6 per cent, and the target is set every five years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Inflation targeting means a central bank aims to keep inflation within a targeted range.
II. The inflation target in India is set by the RBI alone, every five years.
III. Retail inflation is required to remain within a mandated band of 2 to 6 per cent.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong because the Government sets the target in consultation with the RBI, while I and III match the booklet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The RBI was established on April 1 in Calcutta.
II. India's inflation target is 6 per cent with a deviation of ±2 per cent.
III. The RBI acts as banker to the government.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while statement II is wrong because the target is 4 per cent.

quizzes.title: Inflation Targeting and the RBI: Short Answer
quizzes.passage: Inflation targeting is a monetary policy framework in which the central bank aims to keep the inflation rate within a range that is defined in advance. In India, the framework has been shaped by committee recommendations and by government decisions taken over time. The target and the permitted band around it are not chosen by the RBI alone. The government sets them in consultation with the Reserve Bank, and the arrangement is reviewed on a regular cycle. The RBI, for its part, works to maintain price stability while promoting economic growth. It carries out several roles in the financial system, and its supervisory functions also cover the issue of bank licences. It acts as the monetary authority of the country and as a supervisor of commercial banks, and it issues and destroys currency notes. It also acts as banker to the government and as the manager of foreign exchange. Retail inflation is watched against a mandated band set under the framework. The RBI was set up after a commission recommended its establishment, and the British government passed the Act that created it. The RBI also serves as lender of last resort for commercial banks. Taken together, these responsibilities place the RBI at the centre of the country's money and banking system.

questions.q: In which year did India adopt Flexible Inflation Targeting?
questions.explanation: India adopted Flexible Inflation Targeting in 2016.

questions.q: What is India's inflation target, in per cent?
questions.explanation: India's inflation target is 4%, with a deviation of plus or minus 2%.

questions.q: Which committee formalised inflation targeting in India in 2014? (name of the committee)
questions.explanation: The Urjit Patel Committee formalised inflation targeting in 2014.

questions.q: In which city was the RBI established on April 1? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the RBI was established on April 1 in Calcutta.

questions.q: The 4% target with a 2% band was first proposed by the Chakravarty Committee during which years? (give the span of years)
questions.explanation: The Chakravarty Committee first proposed the target during 1982-85.

questions.q: Once every how many years is the inflation target set by the Government in consultation with the RBI? (number of years)
questions.explanation: The inflation target is set every 5 years under the amended RBI Act, 1934.

questions.q: Retail inflation is required to stay within a mandated band of what range, in per cent?
questions.explanation: Retail inflation is within the mandated target band of 2 to 6 per cent.
